Actual Article Body:
A provocative claim by Ambassador David Perdue that Donald Trump offered to sell weapons to Xi Jinping has ignited debate over the transactional nature of U.S.-Pacific security policy.

The geopolitical landscape of U.S.-China relations hit a jolt following comments from U.S. Ambassador David Perdue. Perdue claimed that during a recent summit in Beijing, President Trump asked President Xi Jinping if China was interested in purchasing American military hardware. This revelation comes at a volatile moment for Taiwan, where a $14 billion arms package is currently held in abeyance—a move Trump has previously characterized as a strategic 'negotiating chip' rather than a fixed security commitment.
